traceability.notes:
The story docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md is a concrete specification for cross-rule error message behavior and conventions.
Implementation across the ruleset matches the story: - All key rules define specific, actionable meta.messages with appropriate placeholders and ESLint-idiomatic messageIds: - traceability/require-story-annotation: missingStory with a clear, imperative message and ESLint suggestions; tests confirm messageId, data ({ name, functionName }) and suggest behavior (REQ-ERROR-SPECIFIC, REQ-ERROR-SUGGESTION, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT, REQ-ERROR-LOCATION). - traceability/require-req-annotation: missingReq uses the {{functionName}} placeholder, explains how to add @req, and is configured as an error, aligning with REQ-ERROR-SPECIFIC, REQ-ERROR-SUGGESTION, REQ-ERROR-SEVERITY. - traceability/require-branch-annotation: missingAnnotation follows the shared branch pattern "Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}.", satisfying branch-related conventions and consistency. - traceability/valid-annotation-format: invalid*Format messages all use the shared "Invalid annotation format: {{details}}." pattern, exposing detailed context about what’s wrong with @story, @req, or @supports content. - traceability/valid-story-reference and traceability/valid-req-reference: messages clearly distinguish missing files, invalid extensions, unsafe paths, filesystem errors, and missing requirement IDs, each including the relevant path/ID placeholders and explanatory wording.
The dedicated story-specific test suite tests/rules/error-reporting.test.ts directly validates the core requirements for require-story-annotation, and the broader rule test suites validate the others. A full Jest run (npm test -- --verbose) passes, including this suite, demonstrating that all specified behaviors remain intact.
The acceptance criteria are therefore satisfied: - Core Functionality & Quality Standards: every validation rule has non-generic, ESLint-style messages via meta.messages and messageIds. - Integration & User Experience: integration tests confirm messages propagate correctly through ESLint CLI and typical usage, and messages include problem description, function/branch context, and suggested fixes where applicable. - Error Handling: valid-story-reference and related helpers distinguish missing files vs filesystem errors and handle boundary cases gracefully; valid-annotation-format surfaces config regex issues via a dedicated invalidRuleConfiguration message. - Documentation: this story itself documents the conventions and current rule implementations, and the code is annotated with @story/@req/@supports tags tying behavior back to the story.
Given the aligned implementations, targeted tests referencing this story, and a passing full test run, this story is fully implemented and currently working as specified.
